scope: Full PR diff (14 files, +2892/−5) saved at diff.patch; 3201 lines > 3000 → chunked: c1 = spec + client (1–2917), c2 = server + shared (2918–3201); one full lens wave per chunk, sequentially. Worktree detached at 9d66ce9.

lenses.execution: 7 panes in dedicated tab w1T:t7T (mm-<lens>-c1-r1 / mm-<lens>-c2-r1), each ran `pi -p --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash --no-session` against its lens brief; all 14 wrote <lens>.json and exited 0. blind isolated (diff-only). All lens panes closed after the wave.

verification.rejected_detail: blind c1[4] (what-happens-next trailing period — UX §7.4 quote has no period inside the quotes; the PR's own spec added one, code matches UX) and blind c1[8] (spec dev-note says batches < 3, code uses < 4 — code is correct: after reminder 1 (3 batches) reminder 2 is still pending, so the line must show; the PR spec's number is the typo).

build_verification: make build OK; make test-client 502 passed; make test-shared 108 passed; make test-server pass (no failures). run at 9d66ce9 in the round worktree.
verdict_reason: 1 blocker: AR-RC13 one-stable-contract — the panel re-implements the terminal-status rule (is_terminal) instead of consuming hooks.can_record_manual shipped in the same payload, and the client set already diverges from the server's (Completed omitted) — the exact re-derivation the briefing guard calls a blocker. The 12-state matrix, §4.2/§7.4 verbatim copy (all 13 §4.2 rows present), pill colours (never red), expand-only back-compat contract (decoders + untouched RC4.1 strip), testids, a11y (region/aria/buttons), and all build/test gates verified green. Warnings: em-dashes in 2 implementer-authored copy strings (ban test doesn't cover refcheck consts), 'landlord' word-map gap rendering raw wire value, relationship_other dropped, form-opened timeline insertion order, gendered 'him', explainer dismissed-state spec drift, character partial count, and the coverage gaps (auto-expand + word-map total-match untested).

findings.title: Panel re-derives terminality client-side (is_terminal) and its set already diverges from the server's (omits Completed) — hooks shipped in the same payload are ignored
findings.detail: AR-RC13: the panel re-implements the server's terminal rule instead of reading hooks.can_record_manual (in the same payload), and diverges — Completed (v2 voice) is terminal server-side but not client-side, so a future voice row breaks the sub-line. Blocker per briefing guard.
findings.recommended_fix: Derive the all-terminal sub-line from the payload hooks: list.all(calls, fn(c) { not c.hooks.can_record_manual }) — one stable contract.

findings.title: Em-dashes in implementer-authored user-facing strings (unmoderated-flag sentence + nudge-failed timeline label) violate the RT CI em-dash ban
findings.evidence: pub const refcheck_unmoderated_flag: String = "Unmoderated referee text — written by the referee, not reviewed by us." / pub const refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed: String = "Applicant nudge — couldn't send" / no_em_dash_test (copy_test.gleam:308) iterates for_each_copy (toast/page codes only) so the new refcheck consts bypass the pin
findings.detail: 4 lenses agree. The spec gives no verbatim copy for these two strings (spec-only: 'flagged as unmoderated referee text'), so the implementer authored them — and shipped em-dashes, banned in user-facing copy. The ban test doesn't reach refcheck consts, so CI stays green.
findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite both strings without em-dashes (e.g. 'Unmoderated referee text. Written by the referee, not reviewed by us.') and extend no_em_dash_test to scan refcheck copy.

findings.title: Key-facts word map keys on phantom wire value 'their_landlord'; the real wire value 'landlord' renders raw in the landlord-facing table
findings.evidence: questions.gleam:125: #("landlord", form_copy.opt_their_landlord), / copy.gleam:750: "their_landlord" -> "Their landlord" / refcheck_choice_word fallback: _ -> value
findings.detail: The landlord relationship question stores wire value "landlord" (the tuple's first element); the word map only maps "their_landlord" (the label's snake_case, never stored). relationship_to_applicant="landlord" renders raw "landlord" in the key-facts table.
findings.recommended_fix: Map "landlord" -> "Their landlord" in refcheck_choice_word (and drop or keep "their_landlord" defensively); add the spec'd total-match word-map test.

findings.title: relationship_other (the referee's verbatim 'Other' relationship text) is never rendered — key-facts shows bare 'Other'
findings.evidence: slot_field_keys comment: 'minus relationship_other — a companion field that renders with its parent "Other" row, never as a standalone question' / server result.gleam:168-172 emits #("relationship_other", str_or_null(draft, "relationship_other")) when relationship == "other" / render_value has no relationship_other arm
findings.detail: The server stores the referee's custom relationship text alongside "other"; the panel's key-facts filter drops it and nothing renders it with the parent row — the landlord sees only 'Other'. The doc comment claims it renders with its parent; no code does.
findings.recommended_fix: Render relationship_other text appended to the 'Other' value (e.g. 'Other — cousin of the applicant') or as its own row.

findings.title: 'Form opened' timeline line is pinned right after the invitation batch even when the form opened after later batches — mini timeline renders out of chronological order
findings.detail: The link stays live, so a referee can open the form after reminder 1 or 2 (e.g. T+50h after a T+48h reminder). The insertion hard-codes position after the invitation; the line order then contradicts the per-line <time> datetimes.
findings.recommended_fix: Insert the form-opened line by comparing timestamps against batch at-values (chronological merge) instead of a fixed slot.

findings.title: Objected-state copy hardcodes 'him' while the referee name is interpolated — misgenders female referees ('Sarah ... asked us not to contact him.')
findings.evidence: pub fn refcheck_state_objected(name, first_name) { name <> " asked us not to contact him. All automated contact has stopped. This tells you nothing about " <> first_name <> ". You can ask " <> first_name <> " for another referee." }
findings.detail: UX §7.4 example uses a male referee (Colm), so 'him' is verbatim in the spec — but the implementer interpolates arbitrary referee names, making the pronoun wrong for female referees in shipped user-facing copy.
findings.recommended_fix: Use the gender-neutral 'them' ('asked us not to contact them') — the payload carries no gender.

findings.title: PR's own spec promises a localStorage-persisted explainer dismissed state (rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed + UserDismissedRefcheckExplainer); the code ships a session-scoped toggle reset on every route change
findings.evidence: spec-rc4-2 OWNS #3: 'refcheck_explainer_dismissed: Bool (hydrated from localStorage rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed)' + Dev Notes 'localStorage hydration mirrors the sweep-nudge pattern... key rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed' / code: refcheck_explainer_open: Bool, reset to False on BrowserChangedUrl; no localStorage, no UserDismissedRefcheckExplainer
findings.detail: UX §7.3 says 'collapsed by default, per-user dismissed state'. The shipped behavior forgets the dismissal on every navigation and every session — the 'per-user dismissed state' is not implemented and the PR's own spec drift is undocumented.
findings.recommended_fix: Either implement localStorage persistence per the PR spec, or amend the spec + UX note documenting the session-scoped decision.

findings.title: Character slot's 'answered {m} of {n}' counts free_text_signals — a field the character form never asks — so a fully-answered character reference reads 'answered 6 of 7'
findings.evidence: character_ref field_keys: [identity_confirmed, relationship, capacity, known_duration, character_statement, would_stand_again, free_text_signals] / server result.gleam character_verification comment: 'the character slot carries no optional free-text question, so the array is empty' / server required_draft_keys CharacterRef has 6 keys (no free text)
findings.detail: The client counts free_text_signals toward n for character (7) although the character form never asks it and the server always emits [] — the honest count is 6. A complete character partial misreads as unfinished.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop free_text_signals from the character slot's field_keys (or exclude it from the total for slots whose form lacks the free-text question).

findings.title: First-view auto-expand + toggle/route-reset update logic has zero coverage; the spec-mandated total-match word-map test is absent (and would have caught the 'landlord' mapping bug)
findings.evidence: client_test.gleam has no update-level refcheck tests (grep UserToggledRefcheck / refcheck_auto_expanded: none); spec Verify says '12-state matrix rendered... word-map tests: every wire value resolves (total match)' — absent; panel tests assert ~5 of ~30 word values
findings.detail: The PR's own testing standard mandates a total-match word-map test; none exists, and the unmapped 'landlord' wire value shipped because of it. The auto-expand state machine (first_view/summary_ids/auto_expanded set) is the PR's only new update logic and is untested.
findings.recommended_fix: Add update-level tests for first-view auto-expand + toggle messages + route reset, and a total-match refcheck_choice_word test over every wire value.

findings.title: status_timestamp's Partial/ManualRecorded arms can never fire — submitted_at is only stamped by complete_reference_call (form_completed); sweep_terminal (partial) never stamps it
findings.evidence: UPDATE reference_call SET status='form_completed', ... submitted_at = now() ... (complete_reference_call.sql) / sweep_terminal UPDATE sets status/outcome/terminal_reason/result but NOT submitted_at
findings.detail: Partial rows therefore render without any timestamp, and the shared doc claim 'or a manual outcome is recorded' is forward-looking only (RC5.1). Harmless but dead branches + an overclaiming doc comment.
findings.recommended_fix: Stamp submitted_at on partial terminalization too, or document that partial rows intentionally show no timestamp.

findings.title: Form-opened timeline <time datetime> carries raw Postgres ::text format (e.g. '2026-08-01 21:12:00+00') — colon-less offset is not a valid HTML datetime value
findings.evidence: COALESCE(form_opened_at::text, '') AS form_opened_at / html.time([attribute("datetime", line.at), ...]) where line.at = form_opened_at for the Form-opened line
findings.detail: Attempts' at-values are RFC3339 (valid); the additive form_opened_at/submitted_at ride Postgres ::text (space separator, '+00' offset). The display formatter handles both, but the datetime attribute is invalid HTML for the Form-opened line.
findings.recommended_fix: Normalise to RFC3339 in the SQL (to_char with ISO format) or format client-side before the datetime attribute.

findings.title: refcheck_off_contacts_label is never referenced
findings.evidence: pub const refcheck_off_contacts_label: String = "Referee details" / grep: no usage anywhere in client/src or client/test
findings.detail: Dead export; the Off state renders chips without the section label.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove the const or render it above the Off-state contact blocks.

findings.title: month_abbr duplicated byte-for-byte (private in copy.gleam and helpers/format.gleam)
findings.evidence: both files define a private fn month_abbr with identical Jan..Dec mapping
findings.detail: Minor DRY violation; both are private so there is no conflict, but the mapping can drift.
findings.recommended_fix: Export helpers/format's month_abbr and reuse it.

findings.title: reference_panel.gleam is 1263 lines — 3× the <400 view-module target, bundling view + JSON decoding + signal thresholds
findings.evidence: 1263 lines; contains view logic, parsed-result decoders (signals/form_session/ai_summary), word renderers, and worth-knowing threshold logic
findings.detail: Guideline-level; the decoders + renderers could move to a helper module (e.g. reference_panel_result.gleam) without changing behaviour.
findings.recommended_fix: Split the result-parsing/render half into a sibling module.

findings.title: Mini-timeline renders unkeyed while the rows list in the same module uses keyed.ul
findings.evidence: html.ul([attribute("role", "list"), ...], list.map(lines, ...)) — no keys, versus keyed.ul for rows
findings.detail: Lustre lists that can grow (attempt batches arrive) should be keyed; the timeline lines have no stable keys today.
findings.recommended_fix: Use keyed.ul with the batch at-timestamp (or index) as key.

findings.title: field_is_answered counts any object as answered while render_value renders 'Not answered' for content-less objects (e.g. period {from, to:''})
findings.evidence: field_is_answered: decode.dict success -> True / render_period: to == "" -> copy.refcheck_not_answered
findings.detail: A partial with an empty period side (from set, to '') counts as answered in 'answered {m} of {n}' but renders 'Not answered' in the table — a small count/display inconsistency.
findings.recommended_fix: Align the answered predicate with the renderers (an object is answered only when it yields a non-'Not answered' render).

findings.title: First-view auto-expand is consumed by the first detail landing even when there was nothing to expand (all rows queued)
findings.evidence: let first_view = !set.contains(model.refcheck_auto_expanded, aid) ... refcheck_auto_expanded: case first_view { True -> set.insert(model.refcheck_auto_expanded, aid) ... } — inserted regardless of summary_ids being []
findings.detail: If the landlord first views the application pre-completion, the aid joins auto_expanded with an empty expansion; when a reference later completes and they return, no auto-expand fires. UX §7.4 intent is first view WITH a summary.
findings.recommended_fix: Only insert into refcheck_auto_expanded when summary_ids is non-empty.

findings.title: 'Never red' test only pins absence of two class tokens (bg-score-red/text-score-red); any other red class would pass
findings.evidence: html |> string.contains("bg-score-red") |> should.be_false / html |> string.contains("text-score-red") |> should.be_false
findings.detail: The pill consts are the real guarantee (teal/slate/navy/amber only) — the test is a weak backstop. A future red class like bg-red-500 would slip through.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the pill_class for each status is one of the four consts (or scan for any /red/ class token).

findings.title: Object-value renderer branches (ongoing/dont_remember/differs/stated/dont_know/different_amount_eur/as_stated) and 6 of 7 worth-knowing signal sentences are untested
findings.evidence: panel tests cover tenancy_period {from,to} + amount {amount_eur} + fast-completion signal only; no fixture exercises ongoing/dont_remember/differs/stated/dont_know/different_amount_eur or the remaining 6 signals
findings.detail: The renderers are pure and cheap to test; the untested branches are exactly where a mapping typo (like the 'landlord' word) hides.
findings.recommended_fix: Add one fixture per object-variant + one per signal sentence (total-match style).

findings.title: Server: empty→null branch for the new columns is unpinned and there is no integration coverage for form_opened_at/submitted_at on the wire
findings.evidence: encode_reference_call_pre_terminal_nullables_test asserts the populated values ride through; no assertion that '' maps to null for the two new fields; integration payload test unchanged
findings.detail: The  -> None mapping is the same pattern as next_attempt_at (tested), so risk is low — but the new columns' wire behaviour has no DB→wire pin.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the nullable test to assert "form_opened_at":null/"submitted_at":null for empty rows, and add the two keys to the integration wire assertion.

findings.title: v2-reserved degradation (Scheduled/Calling/Completed), malformed result JSON, and aria-expanded='true' are untested
findings.evidence: status_pill has Scheduled/Calling/Completed arms; view_completed json.parse Error -> element.none(); tests only assert aria-expanded="false"
findings.detail: Small P3 gaps: the v2 arms are defensive, the parse-error path is silent degradation, and the expanded-state aria attribute flip is unpinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Add 3 small tests (v2 pills render, malformed result renders empty detail, aria-expanded true on expand).

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS (demoted from the lens's FAIL — repo convention rejects coverage-ladder gating)
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md: 'Coverage percentages, tier ladders, and "every function needs a test" rules are not useful here.' / lens gate FAIL based on P1 gaps above
findings.detail: The named P1 gaps above (auto-expand untested, word-map total-match absent) are real and worth fixing; the percentage-ladder FAIL is demoted per project convention.
findings.recommended_fix: Close the named gaps; no percentage target needed.
